domain_label: California / Turlock Knitwear — Consumer, Positioning & Naming Model
purpose: A method for reasoning about who the AI-designed D2C knitwear consumer actually is, how to reach them at a contribution margin that survives a paid-social CAC, how to position the 3-article line (A1 cotton-blend core, A2 fine-acrylic value, A3 merino/lambswool premium) against fast-fashion and premium without fighting on the axis it loses, and how to name and clear a brand that can be owned and registered — without ever naming a real athlete, celebrity, event or meme as the house brand, and without hardening any volatile duty, CAC or price band into a forecast.
assumptions: no observed performance data for this brand exists; every CAC, returns, conversion, price-band and duty figure is a labeled estimate or a dated public fact, never a claim of this brand's realized number

the geography forces a two-market posture: Turlock (~72.9k, ~46.1% Hispanic, CSU Stanislaus ~10,577 students) is the near-zero-CAC in-person seed; the ship-to-California social shopper is the only real scale, and there contribution-margin-after-CAC is the single kill-risk

demographic, legal and fee figures (Turlock population/ancestry/income, California Civil Code 3344/3344.1, Lanham 43(a), USPTO 2025 fees, US sweater duty lines) are cited public facts carried with their honesty tag, not invented

the price ladder (A2 ~$45-65 / A1 ~$70-95 / A3 ~$120-180, AOV target >~$90) is positioning judgment, not a margin model; T9 unit-economics governs the live landed-cost floors and the CAC viability verdict

US sweater MFN duty is cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5%, wool 6110.11 ~16%, acrylic/MMF 6110.30.30 ~32%; the India surcharge on top is volatile and de-minimis is repealed, so every PO is re-priced at the live rate and the entire trajectory is a snapshot
exclusions: the full landed-cost stack, the contribution-after-CAC P&L and the go/no-go duty math (those are the T9 unit-economics deliverable; this layer carries only the positioning-relevant inputs)

the AI-design pipeline mechanics, the line plan matrix, the brand identity system (palette/type/photography) and final candidate names (those are the T8 design and final T7 brand-identity deliverables)
stating a fabricated national TAM/SAM for the ship-to-California knit shopper, or a final brand name before the clearance gate is run — both are refused rather than invented
naming a real athlete, celebrity, nickname, team, league or event as the house brand, a drop or a SKU — a hard legal no, not a creative option
the yarn/finishing pilling-grade derivation and the manufacturing make-vs-buy decision (those are the T2/T6 and T4 deliverables; this layer inherits only the consumer-facing no-pill promise gate)

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GO_TO_MARKET_VERDICT composes the local-seed-to-social-scale posture, organic-heavy CAC discipline, premium-and-bundle AOV, the never-out-cheap/never-out-luxury positioning and the original-coined-name-only rule into a launch sequence, conditioned on pinning the HYPE_SIGNAL_GAP before any name or content ships

glossary.definition: The binding posture of this plan: seed the first 200-500 customers in Turlock at near-zero CAC and fix the size curve in person, then scale only on the ship-to-California social shopper, where contribution margin after a paid-social CAC is the single kill-risk.

Price minus all variable costs including landed COGS, payment fees, ship-to-customer, returns and variable CAC; per the shared glossary it, not gross margin, is the D2C viability test, with LTV:CAC > ~3 the survival bar.

glossary.term: promise the gate, never a percent
glossary.definition: The no-pill honesty rule: market the contractual ICI pilling-box >=3-4 post-wash gate as a pass/fail consumer promise, never a fabricated number like 'cuts pilling 40%', because a single public pilling video is brand-ending for the acrylic A2.

An original coined, arbitrary or suggestive wordmark that captures California/youth/sport-adjacent energy in its rhythm and palette without referencing any real person, team, league, event or meme, so it is registrable and ownable rather than licensable or suable.

The architecture rule that transient youth/hype energy (the A2 acrylic capsule) sits at the front as acquisition while the durable margin-bearing thing (the A1 cotton core) sits behind it and must be protected; if the front door becomes the house brand, both margin and longevity erode.

Fitting garments in person at Turlock pop-ups to learn the real size distribution, which buys down the online return rate (returns run far higher online, ~24% vs ~6% in-store) before the brand scales on social.

The four bodies of law that stack on a real-identity brand name: California Civil Code 3344 (with prevailing-party attorneys' fees), 3344.1 (70-year post-mortem descendible right), Lanham 43(a) false endorsement (no registration needed to sue), and Class-25 apparel trademark; any one is enough to lose.
Apparel is USPTO Class 25 and online retail is Class 35; the office treats them as coordinated for likelihood-of-confusion, so a knitwear D2C mark must be cleared in both, not just one.

Any India-to-US sweater duty figure (MFN base plus the volatile post-2025 India surcharge) is true only at a point in time; de-minimis is repealed and the surcharge moves, so the rate is re-confirmed at every PO and never hardened into a forecast.

What is actually trending for Central-Valley youth in 2026 and where they get news is an UNKNOWN owned by no upstream file, yet it is the live input both a hype-adjacent name and trend-native content require; it must be pinned before a name or content calendar ships.

nodes.definition: Establish the posture the whole plan hangs off: the geography forces a two-market split with one posture, local-seed to social-scale. Design for only one market and the brand forfeits either cheap trust (skip Turlock) or all its reach (skip social). Turlock (~72.9k, value-conscious college town) is the near-zero-CAC, in-person, high-trust seed that buys the first 200-500 customers and fixes the size curve; the ship-to-California social shopper, who discovers product on TikTok FYP / Instagram Reels / Pinterest, is the only path to meaningful scale, and is exactly where contribution margin after CAC becomes the single kill-risk. This is the size and shape of the consumer before any channel, price or naming question is asked.

included: the two-market split and the one-posture rule
the seed-vs-scale economic roles
where each consumer gets news

pros.claim: Naming the seed-to-scale posture stops the plan from optimizing one market and forfeiting the other
pros.example: a Turlock-only plan keeps cheap trust but never reaches the social shopper where the business actually exists

cons.claim: A two-market posture invites running two brands at once and diluting both
cons.example: an in-person Turlock voice and a TikTok-native voice drifting apart until neither converts

failure_modes: treating the Turlock SAM as the business and never building for social scale
building only for social and skipping the in-person size-curve and trust the seed provides
acceptance_tests: the posture states the two markets, the one-posture rule, each consumer's news source, and the seed-vs-scale economic role with cited Turlock figures
revisit_triggers: the social discovery surface (TikTok/IG/Pinterest) shifts materially
the Turlock seed channel access changes
a measured California SAM appears

base.update_signal: a discovery surface, seed-channel access, or SAM figure changes

nodes.definition: Model Turlock as the seed, not the business. Population ~72,900; Hispanic 46.1% / White 41.5% / Asian 5.6%, with Portuguese 7.3% and Assyrian 6.1% communities; median household income ~$82,995 (2024); CSU Stanislaus ~10,577 students (~9,244 undergrad). A value-conscious college town is the cheapest place on earth for this brand to acquire its first 200-500 customers at near-zero CAC (pop-ups, weekend markets, CSU channels, the community graph) and to fix the size curve in person, every offline fitting buying down the online return rate. The ~46.1% Hispanic share makes a Spanish-language reading of any name and tagline mandatory, not optional polish. The local serviceable market is an order-of-magnitude 'small' (placeholder-share arithmetic lands ~$50k-$110k/yr; keep only the order of magnitude), which is precisely why Turlock is a seed and the social shopper is the scale.

skipping the mandatory Spanish-language name read in a ~46% Hispanic market
wasting the in-person window without capturing the size curve

nodes.definition: Lay down the single viability test the whole plan turns on: per the shared glossary, contribution margin after CAC, not gross margin, decides D2C survival, with LTV:CAC > ~3 the bar. The governing number is blended CAC: organic-heavy runs ~$20-30 while paid-only runs ~$75, and paid-only acquisition at a sub-$90 AOV does not survive the contribution math (a CAC the same order of magnitude as the whole gross margin). This is why the entire plan assumes the brand stays organic-heavy; the contribution math, not factory cost, is the kill-risk, and the realistic CAC band is an estimate that one live ad test would harden or collapse. These are niche-blended industry compilations, direction solid and magnitude soft, not this brand's numbers.

organic ~$20-30 vs paid-only ~$75 blended CAC
why paid-only at sub-$90 AOV fails
excluded: the channel mechanics that hold CAC down

pros.example: an 80% gross sweater still losing money once a $45-70 paid CAC is subtracted from a single-unit order

cons.claim: The CAC band is an un-cross-examined industry estimate, so the whole verdict rests on a soft governing number
cons.example: a realistic CAC that a single $1-2k ad test could move enough to flip the per-order verdict

failure_modes: judging the brand on gross margin and ignoring CAC
hardening the estimated CAC band into a forecast without a live test

acceptance_tests: the kill-risk states contribution-after-CAC as the test, the LTV:CAC > ~3 bar, the organic-vs-paid CAC bands, and the sub-$90-AOV paid-only failure, all labeled estimate
revisit_triggers: a live ad-account CAC test is run
the AOV or contribution structure changes
the LTV:CAC survival rule is revised

base.update_signal: a live CAC test, an AOV change, or the LTV:CAC rule changes

nodes.definition: Define the channel ladder that follows the two-market split. Seed channels (cheap/local/trust): pop-ups, weekend/farmers markets, CSU Stanislaus, the community graph, delivering first customers plus in-person fit calibration. Scale channels (owned + organic) carry the load: organic IG/TikTok content + a Shopify-owned hub + an email/SMS list. Paid social only amplifies proven content; it never buys cold customers at a sub-$90 AOV. Marketplaces are secondary and article-specific: Etsy / TikTok-Shop for the youth A2 capsule, Amazon only for a basic A1/A2 cash line, and never A3 on Amazon because it commoditises the premium/AI story; Faire/boutique wholesale is piloted only once T9 confirms a wholesale margin floor. The channel ladder is what operationalizes the organic-heavy CAC discipline.

marketplaces as secondary and article-specific with never-A3-on-Amazon
wholesale gated on a T9 margin floor

pros.claim: A tiered ladder makes the organic-heavy CAC discipline concrete instead of aspirational
pros.example: organic IG/TikTok plus a Shopify hub and email/SMS carrying the load while paid only amplifies a proven post

cons.claim: Organic-load-bearing reach is slow and unpredictable, so the ladder can under-deliver volume early
cons.example: a content engine that takes months to compound while fixed costs run

failure_modes: using paid social to buy cold customers at a sub-$90 AOV
putting A3 on Amazon and commoditising the premium story
piloting wholesale before T9 confirms the margin floor
acceptance_tests: the ladder states the seed, scale and amplify tiers, the article-specific marketplace rule with never-A3-on-Amazon, and the T9-gated wholesale pilot
revisit_triggers: a discovery or marketplace channel's economics shift
a T9 wholesale margin floor is confirmed
paid-social efficiency changes materially

base.update_signal: a channel's economics, the wholesale floor, or paid-social efficiency changes

These bands are downgraded positioning anchors, not a forecast; the live floors are owned by T9.

nodes.definition: Define the one move that creates CAC headroom: bundle to push AOV above ~$90 (toward the ~$120-150 that makes the model robust). CAC and outbound shipping are charged per order, not per unit, so a 2-unit bundle or a single premium unit amortises one CAC and one ship over a bigger basket, turning an order that dies at single-unit value into one that survives a realistic CAC. The central pricing instruction back to T8 line planning is to sell the line in baskets (two mid-tier pieces or one A3 premium) rather than as standalone sub-$90 sweaters, which is exactly why A2 is a basket-filler and not a standalone hero. The exact AOV-to-contribution arithmetic is owned by T9; this node carries the positioning instruction.

nodes.definition: Carry the policy facts that re-floor the price ladder and the operating model. Corrected US sweater MFN duties: cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5%, wool 6110.11 ~16%, acrylic/MMF 6110.30.30 ~32% (the earlier 'cotton ~7%' figure was wrong and is corrected here). The <$800 de-minimis exemption is repealed (suspended for all countries effective Aug 29, 2025; ad-valorem duty on postal shipments from Feb 28, 2026), so duty-free drop-ship is dead and bulk-import-then-US-fulfill is the structurally correct model (which also dents the fast-fashion direct-import edge). The India surcharge layered on top of MFN is high and volatile, a moving trajectory treated entirely as a snapshot and re-priced at every PO. The only forward-valid facts are that de-minimis is repealed and duty is high and volatile; the live floors and the contribution verdict are owned by T9.

nodes.definition: Position against fast-fashion (Shein/H&M-tier) on the axis the brand can win and never on the one it loses. Win on durability, fit, no-pill, story and local trust; never on price, because the brand cannot and must not out-cheap fast-fashion. This is the front half of the split-the-field rule: a sub-$90, fit-honest, no-pill, locally-trusted, AI-design-storied sweater beats a $20 disposable one on everything except sticker price, and competing on sticker price is a guaranteed loss. The dead de-minimis also dents the fast-fashion direct-import cost edge, narrowing the only axis on which they were unbeatable.

base.update_signal: a fast-fashion quality/local move or the import-cost edge changes

nodes.definition: Position against premium (Everlane / Quince / J.Crew-tier) on the axis the brand can win and never on the one it loses. Win on price-for-quality, AI-design novelty, local authenticity and limited drops; never try to out-luxury them. This is the back half of the split-the-field rule: the brand offers a credibly-made, no-pill sweater with a genuinely novel AI-design story and a Turlock-local identity at a price below heritage premium, using drops to manufacture scarcity and urgency. Attempting to out-luxury established premium on materials, heritage or price-up is a guaranteed loss; the winning lane is more-novel-and-local-for-less, anchored by the A3 halo.

nodes.definition: Name the three story pillars both analysts independently reached. (3) 'From Turlock, for the way California actually dresses' - converts the warm-climate constraint into a locally-ownable asset that reads clean/light/Californian, never alpine/heritage-wool.

nodes.definition: State the architecture rule both halves of the analysis converge on: transient/youth/hype energy goes at the front as acquisition, and the durable, defensible, margin-bearing thing sits behind it and must be protected. The A2 youth capsule is the front door, not the margin (Gen-Z is the most price-sensitive, highest-return cohort, so its job is reach/UGC, not contribution), while the A1 cotton core is the margin-bearing thing behind it. Watch the dial: if the youth capsule visually or verbally becomes the house brand, both the margin and the brand's longevity erode. The identity must not hard-code a fibre or a season, because the warm climate already demotes wool to a thin capsule; the house brand must outlive any one article.

the watch-the-dial erosion warning
the no-fibre/no-season identity constraint

pros.claim: The front-vs-behind rule protects the margin-bearing core from being consumed by the acquisition capsule

hard-coding a fibre or season into the identity the climate cannot support

nodes.definition: Model A1, the cotton-blend 12GG 12-month core, as the margin and LTV engine, with its engine status resting on demand and brand-honesty grounds, NOT a duty edge. Indicative MSRP ~$70-95. Its center-of-gravity status rests on the longest sell-window (~Sept-April), the best repeat-purchase LTV, and the no-prickle/no-pill consumer promise that fits the warm California market; its base duty (~16.5%, 6110.20.20) is comparable to wool (~16%), so there is no duty advantage to claim, and acrylic/MMF (~32%) is the article the border penalizes. As a chief-weight-classified blend, the cotton share must stay above 50% or the same sweater becomes MMF at ~32%, so blend % and tolerance belong in every PO (the duty mechanics are owned by T9). The cotton core is the article the brand should build repeat purchase and LTV around.

the sell-window/LTV/no-prickle basis, not a duty edge
the chief-weight blend caveat handed to T9

pros.claim: Grounding the engine in sell-window, LTV and the no-prickle promise gives an honest, defensible center of gravity
pros.example: a ~Sept-April cotton core driving repeat purchase that a seasonal wool capsule cannot

cons.claim: Cotton's no-duty-edge means its engine status depends entirely on repeat behavior that is unproven for a new brand
cons.example: the cotton core failing to clear LTV:CAC > 3 if repeat purchase never materializes

failure_modes: claiming a cotton duty advantage that does not exist (~16.5% ~ wool ~16%)
letting a supplier under-blend cotton below 50% and flip the duty to ~32% MMF
assuming repeat purchase without earning it
acceptance_tests: the model states A1's ~$70-95 band, its engine basis in sell-window/LTV/no-prickle not a duty edge, and the chief-weight blend caveat for the PO
revisit_triggers: the cotton sell-window or repeat-purchase signal changes

base.update_signal: the sell-window, repeat signal, or cotton/MMF duty spread changes

nodes.definition: Model A2, the fine-acrylic 7-12GG value article, as the youth acquisition front door, not the margin. Indicative MSRP ~$45-65. Its job is reach and UGC from the most price-sensitive, highest-return Gen-Z cohort, not contribution: at a sub-$90 standalone price against the realistic CAC it cannot pay for its own customer, and acrylic/MMF carries the ~32% duty the border penalizes, so its factory-gate cost lead does not survive landed. A2 is therefore best used as a deliberate basket-filler inside bundles and a front-door acquisition piece, never a standalone hero. It is also the article most exposed to a public pilling failure, so the no-pill gate (promise the gate, never a %) matters most here.

the basket-filler-not-standalone-hero rule
the ~32% MMF duty and pilling exposure

cons.claim: A2's low price and ~32% duty mean it loses money standalone, so over-leaning on it drains cash

acceptance_tests: the model states A2's ~$45-65 band, its reach/UGC front-door role, the basket-filler-not-hero rule, and the ~32% MMF duty and pilling exposure

nodes.definition: Model the size curve and the return-rate gap as the bridge from the Turlock seed to scale. Return rate runs ~24% online versus ~6% in-store; hold the gap (online much greater than offline is robust) rather than the exact decimal, and split it by article and by size, since the size curve is unknown until pop-ups run. The in-person Turlock seed exists in part to fix this: every garment fitted offline calibrates the real size distribution and buys down the online return rate before the brand scales on social. A fine-gauge, fit-sensitive sweater is a high-return category by nature, so the size-curve fix is not a nicety but a direct contribution-margin lever; the realized return rate for these specific constructions is UNKNOWN until the brand sells.

the in-person size-curve fix and its return-rate payoff
splitting returns by article and size

pros.claim: Treating the size-curve fix as a contribution lever ties the in-person seed directly to online survival
pros.example: offline fittings calibrating the size curve and buying down the high online return rate before scaling

cons.claim: The return rate for these constructions is UNKNOWN until selling, so the lever's size is soft
cons.example: a fine-gauge fit-sensitivity pushing returns above the carried ~24% in ways pop-ups cannot fully predict

failure_modes: hardening the ~24% decimal instead of holding the robust gap
scaling on social before the size curve is calibrated in person
treating returns as one rate rather than splitting by article and size
acceptance_tests: the model states the online-vs-in-store return gap (hold the gap not the decimal), the in-person size-curve fix as a contribution lever, and the by-article/by-size split, all as estimates until selling
revisit_triggers: pop-up fittings produce a real size curve
first-cohort return data by article/size appears
a construction's fit-sensitivity changes

base.update_signal: a pop-up size curve, first-cohort return data, or a construction fit change appears

nodes.definition: State the blunt legal verdict: do NOT name the brand, a drop or a SKU after a real athlete, celebrity, nickname, team, league or event. Four independent bodies of law stack, and any one is enough to lose. (1) California Civil Code 3344 right of publicity: knowing commercial use of a person's name/likeness/identity triggers the greater of $750 or actual damages, PLUS the infringer's profits, PLUS punitives, PLUS - decisively - the prevailing party's attorneys' fees, a fee-shift that can exceed the entire line's margin. (2) 3344.1 post-mortem right, descendible 70 years after death, so a dead athlete is not a safe harbor. (3) Lanham Act 43(a) false endorsement: implying a sponsorship that does not exist is actionable with no trademark registration required to sue. (4) Class-25 apparel trademark: athletes register and enforce their names/nicknames (the Giannis 'Greek Freak' matter settled for a reported ~$2M). NIL closes the 'just a local kid' loophole, post-mortem closes the 'they're dead' loophole, and a meme/event carries trademark plus transience risk; at most a cleared, non-identity, non-protected reference can be a drop name, never the house brand.

included: the four-law stack (3344, 3344.1, Lanham 43(a), Class-25)
the NIL/post-mortem/meme loophole closures and the Giannis anchor
the drop-name-at-most carve-out for a cleared non-identity reference
excluded: the safe coined-name path (its own node)

pros.claim: Stacking the four laws shows any one is enough to lose, justifying extreme conservatism on real-identity names
pros.example: the 3344 prevailing-party attorneys' fee-shift alone exceeding the line's margin if the brand loses

cons.claim: Whether a given local athlete would actually sue a micro-brand is an estimate, so the rule is risk-management not a certainty of suit
cons.example: a local NIL athlete who might not sue, yet still legally could and enforce

failure_modes: naming the house brand or a SKU after a real athlete/celebrity/event/meme
treating a dead or local-college figure as a safe harbor
letting an un-cleared meme reference become more than a drop name
acceptance_tests: the verdict states the four-law stack with the 3344 fee-shift, the 3344.1 70-year right, Lanham 43(a) no-registration-needed, Class-25 marks, the NIL/dead/meme loophole closures and the Giannis ~$2M anchor
revisit_triggers: a relevant right-of-publicity or Lanham ruling changes the exposure
NIL law shifts
a candidate flirts with a real-identity reference

base.update_signal: a publicity/Lanham ruling, NIL law, or a candidate's real-identity flirtation changes

nodes.definition: Define the safe path: put the energy (California / youth / sport-adjacent / current-hype) into an original coined, arbitrary or suggestive wordmark plus palette plus drop-naming convention that the brand can own and register, with transient hype quarantined to cleared drop names. The evergreen house brand is original and defensible; this is exactly what gives a mark that can be registered under 1(b), defended and built LTV on, the opposite of a borrowed name that can be yanked or sued. Illustrative directions, not finalists: coined/abstract Californian (arbitrary, maximally registrable); suggestive climate-true (evokes light/clean/California-everyday knitwear without naming a fibre or season); sport-/hype-ADJACENT energy with zero identity (the vibe in the rhythm of the wordmark, not a licensable name); and process/AI-native. A final name is deliberately UNKNOWN here, because naming it before clearance is the exact mistake to prevent.

included: the original coined hype-ADJACENT ownable wordmark with quarantined drop names
the registrability/defensibility/LTV rationale
the illustrative naming directions and the refused final name

pros.claim: An original coined hype-adjacent mark captures the energy while staying ownable and registrable
pros.example: an arbitrary warm-coast portmanteau that reads Californian but means nothing someone else owns

cons.claim: A fully coined name carries no built-in meaning, so it needs marketing investment to become legible
cons.example: an abstract wordmark that is maximally registrable but requires spend to teach the consumer

failure_modes: naming a final brand before the clearance gate runs
letting transient hype into the house brand rather than quarantining it to cleared drops
choosing a name that reads as a borrowed identity
acceptance_tests: the path states the original coined hype-ADJACENT ownable wordmark, the quarantined-drop-name convention, the registrability/LTV rationale, the illustrative directions, and the deliberately-UNKNOWN final name
revisit_triggers: candidate names exist and need lane confirmation

nodes.definition: Define the gate every candidate name must pass, in order: (1) USPTO knockout search (Trademark Search / TESS-II) for identical and near-identical marks; (2) clear coordinated classes 25 (apparel) and 35 (online retail), which the USPTO treats as coordinated for likelihood-of-confusion; (3) likelihood-of-confusion analysis on sound, look and meaning, not just spelling; (4) common-law plus handle/state sweep for unregistered users, entity names and social handles; (5) domain + social availability, with .com + Instagram + TikTok all ownable; (6) a mandatory Spanish-language reading given the ~46% Hispanic Central Valley, a name that reads badly in Spanish being dead on arrival; (7) a professional full search by an IP attorney before filing; (8) file a 1(b) intent-to-use application EARLY to lock priority before the launch drop. Cost: USPTO 2025 base ~$350/class; attorney-filed ~$1,000-$2,500 (estimate); TM on adoption, R only after registration; ~12-18 months to register.

included: the in-order clearance steps and the mandatory Spanish read
the coordinated classes 25+35 and sound/look/meaning analysis
the .com+IG+TikTok sweep, the file-1(b)-early step, and the cost/timeline
excluded: the legal hard-no rationale (its own node)
the choice of which direction to clear

pros.claim: An ordered gate with a mandatory Spanish read clears a mark the brand can actually own before a drop ships
pros.example: filing 1(b) early to lock priority before the launch drop has sold a single unit

cons.claim: The ~12-18 month registration timeline and attorney cost mean clearance must start well before launch
cons.example: a brand wanting to launch fast colliding with a multi-month registration runway

failure_modes: skipping the mandatory Spanish read in a ~46% Hispanic market
clearing only class 25 and missing coordinated class 35
launching a drop before filing 1(b) and losing priority
acceptance_tests: the gate lists the in-order steps (knockout, classes 25+35, sound/look/meaning, common-law/handle sweep, .com+IG+TikTok, Spanish read, pro search, file 1(b) early) and the ~$350/class + ~$1-2.5k attorney cost and ~12-18mo timeline

a candidate fails a step and needs re-routing
the launch-drop timeline moves against the registration runway

base.update_signal: a USPTO fee/ID-Manual change, a failed clearance step, or the launch timeline changes

nodes.definition: Surface the cross-file gap owned by no upstream file: what is actually trending for Central-Valley youth in 2026, and where exactly they get news, is genuinely UNKNOWN, yet it is the live input both a hype-adjacent name and trend-native content require. The demand side treats it as a translation problem and the naming side hands it back, so no file pins it. This is a first-class open question, not a footnote: a hype-adjacent wordmark cannot be finalized and a content calendar cannot ship until the live trend signal is pinned (flagged for the trend-ingestion pass / T8). Pinning it is a precondition gate on both naming and content, and it is deliberately carried as UNKNOWN rather than fabricated.

its role as a precondition for naming and content
the hand-off to the trend-ingestion pass / T8
excluded: the actual trend content (not knowable here)
the naming and content mechanics themselves

pros.claim: Naming the gap as a precondition stops a name or content calendar from shipping on a guessed trend
pros.example: holding the hype-adjacent finalist until the 2026 Central-Valley-youth signal is actually pinned

cons.claim: An unowned UNKNOWN can stall the plan if no pass is assigned to pin it
cons.example: naming and content both blocked because no file takes ownership of the trend signal

failure_modes: shipping a name or content calendar on a guessed trend signal
leaving the gap unowned so no pass pins it

acceptance_tests: the gap is carried as a first-class UNKNOWN, named as a precondition for naming and content, and handed to the trend-ingestion pass / T8
revisit_triggers: the trend-ingestion pass or T8 pins the 2026 signal

nodes.definition: Name the numbers that decide survival, direction solid and magnitude soft, as niche-blended industry compilations and not this brand's numbers: blended CAC (organic-heavy ~$20-30 vs paid-only ~$75); contribution margin (DTC drifted ~35% to ~22%, 2021 to 2025, industry-wide, so contribution after CAC, not gross margin, is the test, LTV:CAC > ~3); conversion ~2-3% apparel and cart-abandon ~70%; return rate ~24% online vs ~6% in-store (hold the gap, split by article and size); A2 pilling sentiment; sell-through by colour (the hero-colour signal, the line is colour-starved at ~2-4 launch colours); pre-order/waitlist depth; and the live duty + de-minimis state every order cycle. nodes.definition: Compose the positioning halves into one defensible posture: split the field (never out-cheap fast-fashion, never out-luxury premium), carry the three story pillars (AI-designed / no-prickle-no-pill promise-the-gate / from-Turlock-for-how-California-dresses), and run the article architecture (A2 youth capsule as the front door, A1 cotton core as the margin engine behind it, A3 merino as the halo anchor) without hard-coding a fibre or season into the identity. nodes.definition: Compose the whole KB into the merged go-to-market verdict, the synthesis everything builds toward. Seed in Turlock (near-zero CAC, in-person, fix the size curve, mandatory Spanish read) and scale on the ship-to-California social shopper, where contribution-after-CAC is the kill-risk, so acquisition must stay organic-heavy (blended CAC < ~$35, never paid-only at sub-$90 AOV). Run the price ladder (A2 ~$45-65 / A1 ~$70-95 / A3 ~$120-180) and bundle to AOV >~$90 toward ~$120-150, leading premium + bundles with A2 as a basket-filler not a standalone hero. Position by splitting the field (never out-cheap fast-fashion, never out-luxury premium) on the three pillars, and use an original coined hype-ADJACENT name only, cleared through classes 25+35 plus a Spanish read and filed 1(b) early. The verdict is conditioned on pinning the hype-signal gap (the 2026 Central-Valley-youth trend signal) before any name or content ships, and on T9 confirming the live landed-cost floors and the CAC viability the contribution math turns on.

conflict_axes.name: seed_market_vs_scale_market
conflict_axes.description: The near-zero-CAC Turlock seed has a small SAM while the ship-to-California social shopper is the only scale but carries the CAC kill-risk; a plan can over-invest in either.
poles: build for the cheap-trust Turlock seed
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use Turlock to seed customers and fix the size curve, then scale on the social shopper; never mistake the seed SAM for the business

conflict_axes.name: positioning_price_vs_contribution_floor
conflict_axes.description: The positioning price bands can sit below what contribution-after-CAC can sustain, tempting a price that loses money on the first order.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat the ladder as positioning judgment T9 must floor against live landed cost plus a realistic CAC; never ship a money-losing band

conflict_axes.name: organic_reach_vs_paid_speed
conflict_axes.description: Organic acquisition holds CAC down but is slow, while paid social is fast but does not survive a sub-$90 AOV; the speed-vs-survival trade.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep acquisition organic-heavy (blended CAC < ~$35) and use paid only to amplify proven content, never to buy cold customers at sub-$90 AOV

conflict_axes.name: youth_front_door_vs_durable_house
conflict_axes.description: The loud A2 youth capsule drives reach but can become the house brand and erode the durable margin core it should sit ahead of.
poles: lean on the youth capsule for reach
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the A2 capsule a front-door acquisition piece and govern the voice so the durable A1 core remains the house brand

conflict_axes.name: borrow_hype_identity_vs_own_the_mark
conflict_axes.description: Borrowing a real athlete/celebrity/event/meme identity captures instant hype but is legally fatal, while an original coined mark is ownable but must be built.
poles: borrow a real-identity name for instant hype
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: put the energy in an original coined hype-ADJACENT wordmark; quarantine any cleared non-identity reference to a drop name and never use a real identity in the house brand

conflict_axes.name: promise_no_pill_vs_overclaim_percent
conflict_axes.description: A no-pill promise is a powerful pillar but over-claiming a defensible percentage on the acrylic A2 invites a brand-ending public pilling failure.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: promise the ICI pilling-box >=3-4 gate as a pass/fail consumer promise, never a fabricated percentage

conflict_axes.name: out_cheap_fast_fashion_vs_durability_axis
conflict_axes.description: A value-conscious base anchors on price, tempting a fight on the price axis the brand cannot win against fast-fashion.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: never compete on sticker price; make durability and no-pill vivid so the value shopper chooses quality over cheap

conflict_axes.name: out_luxury_premium_vs_novelty_local_lane
conflict_axes.description: Premium incumbents have heritage and materials depth, tempting an out-luxury fight the brand loses instead of the novelty/local lane it wins.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: never out-luxury established premium; lead with genuine AI-design novelty, local authenticity and limited drops at a price below heritage premium

conflict_axes.name: harden_duty_number_vs_treat_as_snapshot
conflict_axes.description: A single India-surcharge or all-in duty number is tempting to forecast, but the trajectory is volatile and de-minimis is repealed, so any figure is a snapshot.
poles: forecast a single forward duty number
treat every rate as a per-PO snapshot
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: carry only the forward-valid facts (de-minimis repealed, duty high and volatile) and re-confirm the live rate at every PO

edge_cases.description: A standalone A2 acrylic sweater is led on cold paid social and loses money on the first order
edge_cases.trigger: a value-led launch makes the sub-$90 acrylic article the paid-social hero
edge_cases.mitigation: lead with premium + bundles, keep A2 a basket-filler, and hold blended CAC organic-heavy below ~$35

edge_cases.description: A public pilling video on the acrylic A2 goes viral and is brand-ending
edge_cases.trigger: the no-pill promise is over-claimed and a customer documents pilling
edge_cases.mitigation: promise only the ICI pilling-box >=3-4 gate as pass/fail, never a percentage, and watch A2 pilling sentiment

edge_cases.description: The brand is named after a real athlete or a hype meme and faces the right-of-publicity / Lanham / trademark stack
edge_cases.trigger: a candidate name borrows a real person/team/event/meme identity for the house brand
edge_cases.mitigation: use an original coined hype-ADJACENT mark, quarantine any cleared non-identity reference to a drop name, and clear before filing

edge_cases.description: A name reads badly in Spanish and is dead on arrival in the ~46% Hispanic Central Valley
edge_cases.trigger: a finalist skips the mandatory Spanish-language reading
edge_cases.mitigation: make the Spanish read a mandatory gate step before any name ships

edge_cases.description: A launch drop ships before a 1(b) intent-to-use filing and priority is lost
edge_cases.trigger: the clearance runway is skipped to launch fast
edge_cases.mitigation: file 1(b) early to lock priority before the launch drop, allowing for the ~12-18 month registration runway

edge_cases.description: The brand scales on social before the in-person size curve is calibrated and online returns spike
edge_cases.trigger: social scale begins before pop-ups fix the size distribution
edge_cases.mitigation: run the Turlock pop-ups to calibrate the size curve and buy down the online return rate before scaling

edge_cases.description: A3 merino is listed on Amazon and the premium/AI halo story is commoditised
edge_cases.trigger: a marketplace push puts the premium capsule on a commodity channel
edge_cases.mitigation: never put A3 on Amazon; keep marketplaces secondary and article-specific

edge_cases.description: A single forward India-surcharge number is hardened into a price model and a policy swing breaks it
edge_cases.trigger: a price ladder is built on one duty figure rather than a per-PO snapshot
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the duty as a snapshot, re-price every PO at the live rate, and carry only the de-minimis-repealed/high-and-volatile facts

edge_cases.description: A name or content calendar ships before the 2026 Central-Valley-youth trend signal is pinned
edge_cases.trigger: the hype-signal gap is left unowned and the plan proceeds on a guess
edge_cases.mitigation: pin the trend signal via the trend-ingestion pass / T8 before any name or content ships

edge_cases.description: Paid social is used to buy cold customers at a sub-$90 AOV and contribution goes negative
edge_cases.trigger: acquisition drifts from organic-heavy to paid-only without raising AOV
edge_cases.mitigation: use paid only to amplify proven content and bundle to AOV >~$90 toward ~$120-150 before any paid spend

edge_cases.description: A supplier under-blends the cotton core below 50% and the sweater flips to ~32% MMF duty under chief-weight
edge_cases.trigger: a cost-down quietly pushes a cotton-blend past 50% man-made fibre
edge_cases.mitigation: write blend % and tolerance into every PO and hand the duty-classification check to T9 as Importer of Record

edge_cases.description: The A2 youth capsule's aesthetic quietly becomes the house brand and the durable margin core erodes
edge_cases.trigger: the front-door capsule is allowed to dominate the brand voice
edge_cases.mitigation: govern the brand voice so the durable cotton core, not the youth capsule, remains the house brand

dominance_rules.rule: Contribution-after-CAC dominates gross margin in any viability call
dominance_rules.rationale: an 80%-plus gross margin still loses money once a realistic CAC is subtracted, so gross margin is not the test
dominance_rules.trigger: a price or article is judged by gross margin alone
dominance_rules.action: subtract the full variable stack including a realistic CAC and judge on contribution, with LTV:CAC > ~3

dominance_rules.rule: The legal hard no dominates any hype-naming temptation
dominance_rules.rationale: the 3344 + 3344.1 + Lanham + Class-25 stack means any one claim can exceed the line's margin
dominance_rules.trigger: a name borrows a real athlete/celebrity/event/meme identity for the house brand
dominance_rules.action: refuse the real-identity name and route to an original coined hype-ADJACENT mark, with cleared non-identity references only as drop names

dominance_rules.rule: The contribution floor dominates the positioning price band
dominance_rules.rationale: the price ladder is positioning judgment, not a margin model, and a band can sit below the live landed-cost-plus-CAC floor
dominance_rules.trigger: a price band is shipped without clearing the T9 floor
dominance_rules.action: hold the ladder against T9's live landed cost plus a realistic CAC and never ship a money-losing band

dominance_rules.rationale: paid-only acquisition at a sub-$90 AOV does not survive the contribution math
dominance_rules.trigger: acquisition leans on cold paid social
dominance_rules.action: keep blended CAC organic-heavy below ~$35 and use paid only to amplify proven content

dominance_rules.rationale: a fabricated percentage on the acrylic A2 invites a brand-ending public pilling failure
dominance_rules.trigger: marketing reaches for a pilling number
dominance_rules.action: promise only the ICI pilling-box >=3-4 pass/fail gate, never a percentage

dominance_rules.rule: The durable house brand dominates the youth front door
dominance_rules.rationale: if the A2 capsule becomes the house brand both margin and longevity erode
dominance_rules.trigger: the youth capsule starts dominating the brand voice
dominance_rules.action: keep A2 a front-door acquisition piece and govern the voice so the durable cotton core remains the house brand

dominance_rules.rule: Premium price, not premium fibre, dominates the customer-payback claim
dominance_rules.rationale: only the A3 price point reliably clears a realistic CAC, the fibre alone does not
dominance_rules.trigger: a premium article's viability is credited to its fibre
dominance_rules.action: attribute the payback to the premium price and anchor the ladder with A3 while leading baskets to ~$120-150 AOV

dominance_rules.rule: The duty snapshot dominates any single forward duty number
dominance_rules.rationale: de-minimis is repealed and the India surcharge is volatile, so any forward figure is a snapshot
dominance_rules.trigger: a price model hardens one forward duty number
dominance_rules.action: carry only the de-minimis-repealed/high-and-volatile facts and re-confirm the live rate at every PO

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set contribution-after-CAC, not gross margin, as the viability test from the first price decision
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a price ladder that looks healthy on gross margin being retracted once a realistic CAC is applied

anti_rework_rules.rule: Route to an original coined hype-ADJACENT name before any real-identity candidate is explored
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a brand name being chosen and then yanked or sued under the right-of-publicity / Lanham / trademark stack

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the mandatory Spanish-language read and file 1(b) before any drop ships
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a name dying on arrival in the Central Valley or losing priority to a launch that preceded the filing

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep A2 a basket-filler and lead premium + bundles from the first line plan
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a value-led acrylic launch that loses money on the first order having to be re-architected

anti_rework_rules.rule: Promise the no-pill gate, never a percentage, in the first marketing copy
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a fabricated anti-pill number triggering a brand-ending pilling video and a returns spike

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the size curve in person at Turlock pop-ups before scaling on social
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an online return-rate spike that an un-calibrated size curve would cause after scale begins

anti_rework_rules.rule: Treat every duty rate as a per-PO snapshot from the first landed-cost pass
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a price model built on a single forward duty number breaking when policy swings

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pin the 2026 Central-Valley-youth trend signal before finalizing a name or a content calendar
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a hype-adjacent name or content plan shipping on a guessed trend and needing to be redone

iteration_protocol.trigger: a live ad-account CAC test produces a real blended CAC
iteration_protocol.action: replace the estimated CAC bands and re-rank the viability of each article and the go-to-market verdict

iteration_protocol.trigger: T9 lands a live landed-cost floor per article
iteration_protocol.action: re-floor the price ladder and the bundle/AOV target against the confirmed contribution math

iteration_protocol.trigger: the India surcharge or a US sweater duty line changes, or de-minimis enforcement shifts
iteration_protocol.action: update the duty floor and re-price the affected articles at the live rate

iteration_protocol.trigger: Turlock pop-ups produce a real size curve or first-cohort return data appears
iteration_protocol.action: replace the carried return gap with by-article/by-size data and update the instrument panel

iteration_protocol.trigger: the trend-ingestion pass / T8 pins the 2026 Central-Valley-youth trend signal
iteration_protocol.action: unblock and finalize the hype-adjacent name lane and the content calendar

iteration_protocol.trigger: a right-of-publicity / Lanham / NIL ruling or USPTO fee/ID-Manual change lands
iteration_protocol.action: re-evaluate the naming hard no and the clearance gate cost/timeline

iteration_protocol.trigger: a Census refresh shifts Turlock demographics or CSU enrollment changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-size the seed market and re-confirm the mandatory Spanish read and CSU seed channel

priority_rationale: The two-market consumer posture, the Turlock seed and the social-scale shopper come first because every channel, price, positioning and naming judgment depends on knowing who the consumer is and where scale and the kill-risk live; the contribution-after-CAC test, the duty floor, the price ladder, the AOV lever and the channel ladder come next because they are the economics that decide whether reaching that consumer survives; the story pillars, the two positioning halves and the three article roles with their architecture then turn the economics into a brand voice; the naming hard no, safe path and clearance gate run in parallel because they decide what the brand can legally be called and own; and the instrument panel, the hype-signal gap, the positioning and naming syntheses, and the merged go-to-market verdict come last because they compose every upstream output into a conditioned launch sequence.
